correctness.rationale: Exact monomial weights give the operator matrix and its holomorphic nuclear rank-one integrand. The integrand bound (1-|z|)^(-1+theta) is rigorously derived in all three beta regimes. Radius-two Banach-valued Cauchy approximation has tail 2*(1/2)^(2m), and positive Gauss–Legendre quadrature cancels Taylor degrees <=2m-1 on every dyadic interval. Summing dyadic errors plus endpoint tail establishes a rank<=Jm trace-norm bound independent of J,m; finite-rank min-max then yields s_n<=C exp(-theta log2 sqrt(n)/2), hence S_p for every p>0. Finite numerical sections are only corroborative.

originality.rationale: Direct primary Theorem 4.2 yields compactness/trace class and p>=1 only; these facts do not entail membership in every p<1 nor a quantitative stretched-exponential approximation rate. The new dyadic analytic quadrature argument supplies both. One-space generalized Hilbert operator and finite structured-matrix comparison theorems do not logically imply this two-weight infinite operator conclusion. Searches identified no matching stronger theorem; residual priority risk from generic analytic-kernel approximation literature remains.
residual_risks: A broad, potentially older theorem on holomorphic curve quadratures for operator ideals could imply a comparable stretched-exponential bound without naming the differential Hilbert operator.
An unindexed quantitative two-weight singular-value paper may exist; search-index absence is not a proof of novelty.
The obtained exponent is not sharp and cannot be compared as an exact spectral invariant.

value.rationale: The direct new 2026 weighted Bergman operator paper gives only compactness, trace class and p>=1. The p<1 membership is a significantly finer regularity conclusion, and constructive low-rank approximants with quadratic logarithmic rank-complexity make the gain quantitative for the entire strict supercritical parameter regime. This is a natural approximation question, not a routine coefficient or isolated arbitrary parameter calculation; optimality is not claimed.
